# 什么是 OAI-SearchBot？

- 原标题：What Is OAI-SearchBot?
- 作者：Flavio Amiel Roborank 创始人
- 原文更新日期：2026-07-15
- 原文：https://roborank.io/glossary/oai-searchbot/
- 栏目：[AI Search & GEO](https://roborank.io/ai-search/)
- 说明：中文全文翻译，后附英文原文。原文中的数据、观点、平台说明及推广内容均按原文保留，未经独立验证。

---

## 中文全文

OAI-SearchBot 是 OpenAI 专门用于索引网页的网络爬虫，使网页能够作为引用来源出现在 ChatGPT 的搜索功能中。它以用户代理标识 OAI-SearchBot 表明身份，与 GPTBot 相互独立：它支持的是 ChatGPT 中的实时搜索可见性，而不是采集用于训练基础模型的内容。

### 核心要点

- OAI-SearchBot 是 OpenAI 三种独立爬虫之一，另外两种是 GPTBot（模型训练）和 ChatGPT-User（用户触发的抓取），每种都有自己的用户代理标识。
- 它的完整用户代理字符串包含 `OAI-SearchBot/1.4`，并链接至 `https://openai.com/searchbot`；在 robots.txt 中屏蔽它，会使网站从 ChatGPT 搜索结果中消失。
- OpenAI 在 `openai.com/searchbot.json` 发布机器可读的 OAI-SearchBot IP 范围列表，方便服务器通过 CIDR 验证请求的真实性。
- 因为它的标识与 GPTBot 不同，你可以允许 OAI-SearchBot 来获得搜索可见性，同时继续禁止 GPTBot 将内容用于训练。

### OAI-SearchBot 如何运作

当有人使用 ChatGPT 内的搜索功能时，答案并非仅凭模型的记忆撰写。ChatGPT 会检索实时网页、读取内容，并引用其中少数页面作为来源。OAI-SearchBot 就是构建和更新这些检索所依赖索引的 [AI 爬虫](https://roborank.io/glossary/ai-crawler/)。如果 OAI-SearchBot 从未抓取过你的页面，那么无论它在 Google 排名多高，都无法成为 ChatGPT 搜索中的引用来源。

OpenAI 运行三种独立爬虫，区分它们正是关键所在。OAI-SearchBot 负责搜索索引。[GPTBot](https://roborank.io/glossary/gptbot/) 收集内容，用于训练基础模型。ChatGPT-User 则在用户或自定义 GPT 触发操作时执行一次性抓取，OpenAI 表示它“不用于自动抓取网络”。三者使用不同的用户代理标识，因此网站可以在 robots.txt 中分别允许或拒绝每一项工作。

OAI-SearchBot 的用户代理字符串包含 `OAI-SearchBot/1.4` 标识和参考网址 `https://openai.com/searchbot`。为了让服务器确认请求是真实的，而不是伪装者冒充的，OpenAI 在 `openai.com/searchbot.json` 发布该爬虫的 IP 范围机器可读文件，其中是一份 CIDR 前缀列表，服务器可据此匹配连接地址。这与 Google 验证 Googlebot 所用的模式相同。

### OpenAI 的三种爬虫

| 标识 | 工作 | 屏蔽的效果 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **OAI-SearchBot** | 为 ChatGPT 搜索结果建立网页索引 | 让你失去 ChatGPT 搜索引用 |
| **GPTBot** | 抓取内容用于训练基础模型 | 将你的内容排除在模型训练数据之外 |
| **ChatGPT-User** | 执行 ChatGPT 或自定义 GPT 中由用户触发的抓取 | 阻止用户要求的按需检索 |

### OAI-SearchBot 示例

OpenAI 自己的机器人文档，最清楚地说明了为什么 OAI-SearchBot 值得在 robots.txt 中单独占一条规则。文档为每种爬虫分配了不同的标识、参考网址和 IP 范围文件：OAI-SearchBot 对应 `openai.com/searchbot.json`，GPTBot 对应 `openai.com/gptbot.json`，ChatGPT-User 对应 `openai.com/chatgpt-user.json`。获取 searchbot 文件后，会得到一个小型 JSON 对象，其中包含 `creationTime` 字段，以及由 `ipv4Prefix` CIDR 网段构成的 `prefixes` 数组——这是服务器可以用来核对请求的具体、可验证列表。

这种区分带来一个直接结果。某出版商在 2023 年为了防止内容档案被用于模型训练，加入 `User-agent: GPTBot` / `Disallow: /`，这并不会影响其 ChatGPT 搜索可见性，因为 OAI-SearchBot 遵循另一个标识，根本未被提及。如今更常见的是反向陷阱：为了阻止训练而写下一条全面禁止的 `User-agent: *` 规则，却也悄悄把网站从 ChatGPT 搜索结果中排除了，因为通配符同样匹配 OAI-SearchBot。

这种行为可以归纳为一个简单规则。既然 OpenAI 将它们记录为三个独立标识，你的 robots.txt 就是三路开关，而不是一个总开关。你可以同时对训练隐身、对搜索完全可见——前提是明确写出各个标识的名称，而不是直接使用通配符。

### 人们常犯的错误

我不断看到这样的错误：团队本来只是想避免自己的文字用于 AI 训练，却在 robots.txt 里写下“User-agent: *”，后面跟着全面禁止规则。这个通配符也会把 OAI-SearchBot 一并扫进去，而后果十分安静：网站就此不再作为来源出现在 ChatGPT 的搜索答案中，没有报错，也没有通知。OpenAI 特意把爬虫拆分成三个具名标识，就是为了让你能够有意识地选择——屏蔽训练爬虫，保留搜索爬虫。把所有 AI 机器人混为一谈，会白白丢掉你原本可能想保留的可见性。明确写出你真正想管理的那个机器人。

### OAI-SearchBot 与 GPTBot 的区别

|  | OAI-SearchBot | GPTBot |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **用途** | 为 ChatGPT 搜索建立网页索引 | 收集内容用于训练基础模型 |
| **用户代理标识** | `OAI-SearchBot` | `GPTBot` |
| **屏蔽的代价** | 失去 ChatGPT 搜索答案中的引用 | 不影响搜索；只排除训练用途 |
| **IP 验证文件** | `openai.com/searchbot.json` | `openai.com/gptbot.json` |
| **与 AI 可见性的关系** | 直接相关——控制搜索收录 | 间接相关——属于权利与训练用途的决策 |

两者常被混淆，因为它们都属于“OpenAI 机器人”，但控制的是不同的结果。屏蔽 GPTBot，是对模型训练表态；屏蔽 OAI-SearchBot，是对能否在 ChatGPT 中被找到表态。分别根据各自用途作决定——参见 [AI 机器人屏蔽](https://roborank.io/glossary/ai-bot-blocking/)，了解指令如何相互作用。

### 常见问题

#### OAI-SearchBot 有什么用途？

OAI-SearchBot 抓取并索引网页，使它们能够作为引用来源出现在 ChatGPT 的搜索功能里。它是面向搜索结果的发现和检索爬虫，不是训练爬虫；正因如此，OpenAI 将它与 GPTBot 分开说明。

#### OAI-SearchBot 和 GPTBot 是同一个东西吗？

不是。它们是不同的爬虫，具有不同的用户代理标识和工作任务。OAI-SearchBot 为 ChatGPT 搜索可见性建立网页索引；GPTBot 收集内容用于训练 OpenAI 的基础模型。屏蔽其中一个不会屏蔽另一个，因此必须在 robots.txt 中分别处理。

#### 我应该在 robots.txt 中屏蔽 OAI-SearchBot 吗？

只有在你不想让自己的页面被 ChatGPT 搜索引用时才应该这样做。屏蔽 OAI-SearchBot 会使你从这一搜索场景中消失。大多数希望获得 AI 搜索可见性的网站会允许它，并另行决定是否屏蔽 GPTBot；后者控制训练用途，而非搜索。

#### 如何验证 OAI-SearchBot 的身份是真的？

将请求的来源 IP 与 OpenAI 在 [openai.com/searchbot.json](http://openai.com/searchbot.json) 发布的范围列表比对。由于恶意行为者可以伪造用户代理字符串，将连接 IP 与 CIDR 列表匹配，才是确认请求确实来自 OAI-SearchBot 的可靠方式。

### 结论

OAI-SearchBot 是 ChatGPT 的搜索爬虫：当有人在 ChatGPT 内搜索时，它决定了你的页面能否被调出并引用。它被刻意设计为不同于 GPTBot 训练爬虫，这意味着你的 robots.txt 可以欢迎带来 AI 搜索可见性的爬虫，同时拒绝为模型训练提供内容的爬虫。

## 英文原文

OAI-SearchBot is OpenAI’s dedicated web crawler that indexes pages so they can appear as cited sources inside ChatGPT’s search feature. Identified by the user-agent token OAI-SearchBot, it is separate from GPTBot: it powers real-time search visibility in ChatGPT rather than collecting content to train foundation models.

### Key Takeaways

- OAI-SearchBot is one of three distinct OpenAI crawlers, alongside GPTBot (model training) and ChatGPT-User (user-triggered fetches), each with its own user-agent token.
- Its full user-agent string identifies as `OAI-SearchBot/1.4` and links to `https://openai.com/searchbot`; blocking it in robots.txt removes a site from ChatGPT search results.
- OpenAI publishes OAI-SearchBot’s IP ranges as a machine-readable list at `openai.com/searchbot.json` so servers can verify authentic requests by CIDR.
- Because it is a separate token from GPTBot, you can allow OAI-SearchBot for search visibility while still blocking GPTBot from training use.

### How OAI-SearchBot Works

When someone uses the search feature inside ChatGPT, the answer is not written from the model’s memory alone. ChatGPT retrieves live web pages, reads them, and cites a handful as sources. OAI-SearchBot is the [AI crawler](https://roborank.io/glossary/ai-crawler/) that builds and refreshes the index those retrievals draw from. If OAI-SearchBot has never fetched your page, that page cannot appear as a cited source in ChatGPT search, no matter how well it ranks in Google.

OpenAI runs three separate crawlers, and the distinction is the whole point. OAI-SearchBot handles search indexing. [GPTBot](https://roborank.io/glossary/gptbot/) collects content to train foundation models. ChatGPT-User makes one-off fetches when a user or a Custom GPT triggers an action, and OpenAI states it is “not used for crawling the web in an automatic fashion.” Each announces itself with a different user-agent token, so a site can permit or refuse each job independently in its robots.txt.

OAI-SearchBot identifies itself with a user-agent string containing the token `OAI-SearchBot/1.4` and the reference URL `https://openai.com/searchbot`. To let servers confirm a request is genuine rather than a spoofed impostor, OpenAI publishes the crawler’s IP ranges as a machine-readable file at `openai.com/searchbot.json` — a list of CIDR prefixes a server can match the connecting address against. This is the same verification pattern Google uses for Googlebot.

### The three OpenAI crawlers

| Token | Job | Blocking effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **OAI-SearchBot** | Indexes pages for ChatGPT search results | Removes you from ChatGPT search citations |
| **GPTBot** | Crawls content to train foundation models | Excludes your content from model training data |
| **ChatGPT-User** | User-triggered fetches from ChatGPT or Custom GPTs | Blocks on-demand retrieval a user asked for |

### Example of OAI-SearchBot

OpenAI’s own bot documentation is the cleanest worked example of why OAI-SearchBot deserves its own line in robots.txt. The docs assign each crawler a distinct token, a distinct reference URL, and a distinct IP-range file: OAI-SearchBot points to `openai.com/searchbot.json`, GPTBot to `openai.com/gptbot.json`, and ChatGPT-User to `openai.com/chatgpt-user.json`. Fetching the searchbot file returns a small JSON object with a `creationTime` field and a `prefixes` array of `ipv4Prefix` CIDR blocks — a concrete, verifiable list a server can check requests against.

That separation has a direct consequence. A publisher who added `User-agent: GPTBot` / `Disallow: /` to keep their archive out of model training in 2023 did nothing to their ChatGPT search visibility, because OAI-SearchBot obeys a different token and was never mentioned. The reverse trap is more common today: a blanket `User-agent: *` disallow, written to stop training, silently also strips the site out of ChatGPT search results, since the wildcard matches OAI-SearchBot as well.

The behavior generalizes into a simple rule. Because OpenAI documents these as three independent tokens, your robots.txt is a three-way switch, not an on/off toggle. You can be invisible to training and fully visible to search at the same time — but only if you write the tokens out by name instead of reaching for the wildcard.

### The thing people get wrong

The error I see constantly is one line in robots.txt that reads "User-agent: *" followed by a blanket disallow, added by a team that only meant to keep their words out of AI training. That single wildcard sweeps up OAI-SearchBot too, and the result is quiet: the site simply stops appearing as a source in ChatGPT’s search answers, with no error and no notification. OpenAI went to the trouble of splitting its crawlers into three named tokens precisely so you could make this choice deliberately — block the trainer, keep the searcher. Treating all AI bots as one bucket throws away visibility you probably wanted to keep. Name the bot you actually mean.

### OAI-SearchBot vs GPTBot

|  | OAI-SearchBot | GPTBot |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Purpose** | Index pages for ChatGPT search | Collect content to train foundation models |
| **User-agent token** | `OAI-SearchBot` | `GPTBot` |
| **What blocking costs you** | Citations in ChatGPT search answers | Nothing in search; only excludes training use |
| **IP verification file** | `openai.com/searchbot.json` | `openai.com/gptbot.json` |
| **Relevant to AI visibility** | Directly — controls search inclusion | Indirectly — a rights/training decision |

The two are frequently confused because both are “OpenAI bots,” but they govern opposite outcomes. Blocking GPTBot is a stance on model training; blocking OAI-SearchBot is a stance on being found in ChatGPT. Decide each on its own terms — see [AI bot blocking](https://roborank.io/glossary/ai-bot-blocking/) for how the directives interact.

### Frequently Asked Questions

#### What is OAI-SearchBot used for?

OAI-SearchBot crawls and indexes web pages so they can surface as cited sources inside ChatGPT’s search feature. It is a discovery and retrieval crawler for search results, not a training crawler, and OpenAI documents it separately from GPTBot for exactly that reason.

#### Is OAI-SearchBot the same as GPTBot?

No. They are different crawlers with different user-agent tokens and jobs. OAI-SearchBot indexes pages for ChatGPT search visibility; GPTBot collects content to train OpenAI’s foundation models. Blocking one does not block the other, so they must be handled separately in robots.txt.

#### Should I block OAI-SearchBot in robots.txt?

Only if you do not want your pages cited in ChatGPT search. Blocking OAI-SearchBot removes you from that surface. Most sites seeking AI-search visibility allow it while separately deciding whether to block GPTBot, which governs training use rather than search.

#### How do I verify OAI-SearchBot is genuine?

Check the request’s source IP against OpenAI’s published range list at [openai.com/searchbot.json](http://openai.com/searchbot.json). Because bad actors can spoof the user-agent string, matching the connecting IP to that CIDR list is the reliable way to confirm a request is authentic OAI-SearchBot traffic.

### The Bottom Line

OAI-SearchBot is the ChatGPT search crawler: the one that determines whether your pages can be pulled up and cited when someone searches inside ChatGPT. It is deliberately distinct from the GPTBot training crawler, which means your robots.txt can welcome the crawler that earns you AI- search visibility while still turning away the one that feeds model training.
